posts.text:
Regulators now expect AI updates to be planned before they ship. They do not yet say what the plan must check.

FDA's final PCCP guidance asks for "pre-defined acceptance criteria" (Section V.A). If "the predefined acceptance criteria for a specific modification are not met", then "the specific modification(s) will not be implemented" (p.27).

The EU AI Act, Art. 43(4), says changes "pre-determined by the provider at the moment of the initial conformity assessment" and documented under Annex IV 2(f) "shall not constitute a substantial modification".

Both require the criterion. Neither says what it must contain.

Often, today:
→ an aggregate score above a threshold
→ no drop against the previous version

What it must contain:
→ paired case-level change, in both directions
→ a repeat-execution baseline, so run-to-run noise is not read as change
→ the evidence the model actually read

Why it matters: in my preregistered, open experiment, five standard retrieval metrics were identical, yet correctness changed in 17.27% of queries. A criterion built on those scores would have approved the update without seeing which cases changed.

My role: I measure what the score leaves undetermined. I turn that into acceptance criteria a named person can sign.

A score is not a decision.

adeebnoor.github.io/ridi

الخلاصة: FDA وقانون الذكاء الاصطناعي الأوروبي يطلبان معايير قبول محددة مسبقاً قبل تحديث النموذج، لكنهما لا يحددان ما يجب أن تتضمنه.
في تجربتي المسجلة مسبقاً بقيت مقاييس الاسترجاع متطابقة، بينما تغيّرت صحة الإجابة في 17.27% من الأسئلة.
المعيار يجب أن يسجّل التغيّر حالةً بحالة، وخط أساس التكرار، والدليل الذي قرأه النموذج.
